knowledge_point.title: Writing First-Order Linear ODEs in Standard Form

question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
2 \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - 2 \cos{(x )}=- 4 y \sin{(x )} + 2\,.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2 \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - 2 \cos{(x )}&=- 4 y \sin{(x )} + 2 \\ 2 \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + 4 y \sin{(x )}&=2 \cos{(x )} + 2 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(2 \sin{(x )})}_{P(x)}y&=\underbrace{\cos{(x )} + 1}_{Q(x)}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=2 \sin{(x )}$ and $Q(x)=\cos{(x )} + 1.$

question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2x-y}{x}\,,\ x\ne 0\,.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=\frac{2x-y}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=\frac{2x}{x}-\frac{y}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\frac{y}{x}&=\frac{2x}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(\frac{1}{x})}_{P(x)}y&=\underbrace{2}_{Q(x)}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=\frac{1}{x}$ and $Q(x)=2.$

question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
\cos{(x )}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\sin{(2 x )}-\sin{(x )}y=0\,,\ \cos{(x )}\ne 0\,.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\cos{(x )}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\sin{(2 x )}-\sin{(x )}y&=0 \\ \cos{(x )}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-\sin{(x )}y&=-\sin{(2 x )} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-(\frac{\sin{(x )}}{\cos{(x )}})y&=-\frac{\sin{(2 x )}}{\cos{(x )}} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-(\tan{(x )})y&=-\frac{2\sin{(x )}\cos{(x )}}{\cos{(x )}} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(- \tan{(x )})}_{P(x)}y&=\underbrace{- 2 \sin{(x )}}_{Q(x)}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=- \tan{(x )}$ and $Q(x)=- 2 \sin{(x )}.$

question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{x}^{2}y=x y^{2}\,,\ y\ne 0\,.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x)\,,
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{x}^{2}y&=x y^{2} \\ y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{x}^{2}y-x y^{2}&=0 \\ y(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{x}^{2}-x y)&=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{x}^{2}-x y&=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(- x)}_{P(x)}y&=\underbrace{- x^{2}}_{Q(x)} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - x y&=- x^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=- x$ and $Q(x)=- x^{2}.$

question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{x+y}{x}\,,\ x\ne 0\,.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x)\,,
$$

where $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ do not depend on $y.$

We have

$$
\begin{aligned}(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=\frac{x+y}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&={x}^{2}(\frac{x+y}{x}) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=x(x+y) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&={x}^{2}+x y \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(- x)}_{P(x)}y&=\underbrace{x^{2}}_{Q(x)} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - x y&=x^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=- x$ and $Q(x)=x^{2}.$

question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
7 y^{2}-ye^{- x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=y\,,\ y\ne 0\,.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x)\,,
$$

where $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ do not depend on $y.$

We have

$$
\begin{aligned}7 y^{2}-ye^{- x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=y \\ -ye^{- x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+7 y^{2}-y&=0 \\ -y(e^{- x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-7 y+1)&=0 \\ e^{- x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-7 y+1&=0 \\ e^{x}(e^{- x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-7 y+1)&=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-7 y e^{x}+e^{x}&=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(- 7 e^{x})}_{P(x)}y&=\underbrace{- e^{x}}_{Q(x)} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - 7 y e^{x}&=- e^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=- 7 e^{x}$ and $Q(x)=- e^{x}.$

question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
7 x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+x y-4 x=4+3 y\,,\ x\ne 0\,.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}7 x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+x y-4 x&=4+3 y \\ 7 x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+(x-3)y&=4+4 x \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(\frac{x - 3}{7 x})}_{P(x)}y&=\underbrace{\frac{4 x + 4}{7 x}}_{Q(x)}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=\frac{x - 3}{7 x}$ and $Q(x)=\frac{4 x + 4}{7 x}.$

$$

A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).

\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+1{y}^{2}(\cos{(2 x )})^{2}&=(6-(1)y\cos{(2 x )})^{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+1{y}^{2}(\cos{(2 x )})^{2}&=36+1{y}^{2}(\cos{(2 x )})^{2}-12 y \cos{(2 x )} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=36-12 y \cos{(2 x )} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(12 \cos{(2 x )})}_{P(x)}y&=\underbrace{36}_{Q(x)}\end{aligned}
